title: Online advertising of compounded glucagon-like peptide-1 receptor agonists
authors: Chetty AK, Chillakanti M, Ramachandran R, Ross JS, Chen AS
population: 79 websites appearing in Google sponsored results that sold compounded semaglutide, tirzepatide or liraglutide or prescriptions for them
funder: not stated in the article text read in PubMed Central; PubMed lists NIH NCATS grant UL1 TR001863.
authorConflicts: Two authors received personal fees from Close Concerns; others report grants from Arnold Ventures, FDA, Johnson and Johnson and NIH outside the submitted work.
result: All 79 websites sold compounded semaglutide and 57 (72.2%) compounded tirzepatide; median first-month price $231 for semaglutide. Eleven (13.9%) did not disclose that the products were compounded and 7 (8.9%) called them generic; 29 (36.7%) stated or implied FDA approval; 39 (49.4%) reported no adverse effects, warnings, precautions or contraindications; 32 (40.5%) made efficacy claims outside the authorised label of the branded drug.
